## Root cause

The `app` Deployment's pod template was changed to `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` (the only delta from the previously working ReplicaSet `app-dcb884b7`). The official nginx image needs writable paths at startup:

```
[emerg] mkdir() "/var/cache/nginx/client_temp" failed (30: Read-only file system)
```

nginx also writes its pid to `/run/nginx.pid` (`pid /run/nginx.pid;` in `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf`). With the root FS read-only, nginx exited 1 → `CrashLoopBackOff`, so the new ReplicaSet never became ready and the rollout stalled at `updatedReplicas: 1`.

I confirmed the entrypoint's `conf.d` warning was *not* the cause — it is non-fatal ("can not modify ... (read-only file system?)" then "Configuration complete; ready for start up" before the fatal mkdir).

## Change

Added two `emptyDir` volumes to the Deployment, mounted at exactly the paths nginx requires, leaving `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` untouched and changing nothing else (image, probe, ports, replicas all preserved):

- `nginx-cache` → `/var/cache/nginx`
- `nginx-run` → `/run`

## Verification (fresh observations)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Replica counts | desired=3, updated=3, ready=3, available=3, unavailable=none; generation 3 == observedGeneration 3 |
| Rollout | `deployment "app" successfully rolled out`; Progressing=True reason=`NewReplicaSetAvailable`; Available=True |
| Pods | all 3 `1/1 Running`, restarts=0, image `docker.io/library/nginx:1.31.5` |
| HTTP through the app | all three pod IPs returned `200` with `<title>Welcome to nginx!</title>`; access log `"GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 896` |
| **Constraint: root FS still read-only** | `touch /should-fail` → `Read-only file system`; `mkdir /nope` → `Read-only file system`; `readOnlyRootFilesystem=true` in the live spec |
| Writable mounts only | `/var/cache/nginx` and `/run` writable; pid file present (`/run/nginx.pid` → `1`) |

The only `Warning` events remaining are the pre-start readiness-probe connection refusals logged before each container began listening (latest ~21s old); there are no new warnings, no restarts, and the deployment reports full availability.
